text:
ACME Support: Hi folks — production mobile app (Android 4.2.1) started returning intermittent 500s about 10:30 UTC. We can't find any request/trace id in the app logs or in the Console. App sits behind our corporate proxy. What exact identifiers do you need and where should we look (SDK, response headers, Console)? We can attach HAR/curl and logs.

Alex (Support): Sorry for the trouble — thanks for reporting. The minimum we need to triage: the API response headers (so we can see the server-side request id), a short curl or HAR that reproduces the 500, and SDK debug logs around the failing call. For us we typically look for: 1) response header 'x-request-id' or 'x-rdw-request-id' (if present), 2) any SDK-generated trace token in the logs (often named 'trace', 'trace_id', or 'trace_token'), and 3) a timestamp and route/path you called.

Maya (SDK Eng): Quick tips to collect from each surface: 
- CURL: run with headers dumped:
  ```
  curl -i -D - -X POST "https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate" \\n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \\n    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n    -d '{\"input\":\"test\"}'
  ```
  The server response headers will print; copy the full header block (we're specifically scanning for x-request-id / x-rdw-request-id).

- HAR (browser/proxy): export the HAR and search for the request to api.redwood.com. Inspect the Response Headers section and copy the exact header lines. HARs are great because they show the full request/response plus timings.

- Android SDK (in-app): enable verbose logging temporarily and reproduce:
  ```java
  // temporary - do not ship this in production
  RedwoodSdk.setLogLevel(RedwoodSdk.LogLevel.DEBUG);
  // reproduce the flow then capture logs (adb logcat -s RedwoodSdk)
  ```
  Look for lines that include 'trace=' or 'trace_id=' or 'trace token'. Also paste the SDK log lines around the error (±5 lines).

- iOS: enable debug logging via the SDK flag or run the app from Xcode and grep for 'trace' in the console output.

Jordan (Platform Eng): A few extra notes because you're behind a proxy: some proxies strip or rewrite headers. Please verify your proxy preserves headers such as x-request-id and Authorization. If the proxy is terminating TLS, the header could be lost before it hits our backend. If you can, reproduce with the mobile device on an open network (or run the same request from a desktop behind the same proxy) to confirm.

Alex (Support): Also — in the Redwood Console you can search for the request id or trace token: Console -> Requests (or Console -> Traces) -> filter by request id / trace token and timeframe. If you share the header lines we can look it up for you. When attaching files, please redact Authorization keys and any PII.

ACME Support: Thanks — attaching a small header snippet we captured from an Android run and a short log paste:
  ```
  HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
  Date: Wed, 12 Apr 2028 10:31:12 GMT
  Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
  Content-Length: 123
  x-request-id: 3f9b2a7c-0d4e-4f6a-9c6b-7a2f9abcd123
  x-server: rw-gw-03
  ```

  SDK log around failure:
  ```
  RedwoodSdk DEBUG: sendRequest url=/v1/generate payload=...
  RedwoodSdk DEBUG: response status=500
  RedwoodSdk DEBUG: responseBody={"error":"internal"} trace=""
  ```

Maya (SDK Eng): Perfect — we have the x-request-id. Can you also run the curl from a machine with the same network path (preferably with -i -D - so headers are printed) and paste the full header block? If the SDK log shows an empty trace token (trace=""), it means the SDK didn't attach a generated trace token on that call — that can happen if the call failed before the SDK could generate it or if logging wasn't capturing the token.

ACME Support: Running curl now, will paste in a minute.

Alex (Support): One more optional debugging trick — if you can add this request header to a repro curl it will force our backend to echo a debug trace token in the response (temporary, safe to use for debugging):
  ```
  -H 'X-Redwood-Debug: 1'
  ```
  That makes it easier for us to correlate without changing your app. Remove it after debugging.

ACME Support: curl output attached, here's the header block we got: x-request-id matches the SDK header above (3f9b2a7c-0d4e-4f6a-9c6b-7a2f9abcd123). We also tried with X-Redwood-Debug and got back a header x-redwood-trace: tkn_abcdef12345

Alex (Support): Thanks — that's ideal. I'm opening an internal ticket and linking the trace: SUP-8942. Can you DM the HAR and the sanitized logs to me (or upload here if preferred)? We'll hand off to Platform for root cause. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Created support ticket SUP-8942 and assigned to Maya + Jordan.

Jordan (Platform Eng): We see the request and the backend 500 at 10:31:12 UTC. Initial hypothesis: a transient downstream dependency timeout. We'll follow up in the ticket with RCA and mitigation. If you can keep the debug header on for one more repro we can attach a full trace that shows where it failed upstream.

ACME Support: Will do, thanks everyone!
